clue.text: Reflection helps those embarking on this escape

definitions.text: Reflection helps those embarking on this escape

parts.words: Reflection helps those embarking on this escape
parts.note: moonlight is sunlight reflected off the moon, and it lights the way for people slipping off by night to dodge their rent or debts

explanation.walkthrough: A MOONLIGHT FLIT is British slang for leaving your home secretly at night, usually to avoid paying rent. 'Reflection' sounds abstract, but it means the moon's reflected light.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for a secret night-time departure that dodges creditors or a landlord, which is exactly an escape.

clue.text: Increased girth of a soldier, according to Jaques?

definitions.text: of a soldier, according to Jaques?
definitions.meaning: in As You Like It, Jaques's seven ages of man put the soldier at the midpoint of life, so his widening is that of the central years

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character describes how a soldier's waist has thickened.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's 'All the world's a stage' speech lists seven ages; the soldier is the fourth, the middle one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the thickening waistline that tends to come in a person's forties and fifties.

clue.text: Eccentric is shot, having turned tail

indicators.note: the tail, the last pair of letters, is turned around while the rest stays put

parts.note: in archery or shooting an outer is a shot hitting the ring outside the bull

explanation.surface: An oddball is done for, having fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned tail' suggests running away, but it swaps the last two letters of OUTER, giving RE. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, from French, means unconventional or bizarre, a synonym for eccentric.

clue.text: Terrible time in grip of fate provided recurring theme

indicators.note: in grip of says the scrambled letters are held inside the word for fate

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of time are mangled into a new order

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A dreadful period under fate's control supplied a theme that keeps returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like a comment on the time, but it is the anagram signal; 'provided' is the conditional word, not 'supplied'.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical or literary motif associated with a character or idea that keeps returning, as in Wagner's operas.

clue.text: Gross woman, one quite far up a tree?

definitions.text: one quite far up a tree?

parts.note: Annie is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A fat woman has climbed some way up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, where a grandmother sits two generations up.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother sits two generations above a child on a family tree, fairly high up it.

clue.text: Sole part thespian initially interpreted

indicators.note: initially asks for only the first letter of thespian

parts.note: to read a situation or text is to interpret it

explanation.surface: An actor first interpreted his only role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole part' suggests an actor's only role, but it is the grooved underside of a shoe's sole.
explanation.definitionFit: The patterned bottom surface of a shoe or tyre that grips the ground.

clue.text: Teach girl badly, lacking energy

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of teach girl are put in a wrong, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone teaches a girl poorly because they are listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and drowsy, short of vigour.

clue.text: Few in number, like snowflakes in moderate fall

definitions.meaning: a light snowfall leaves only a sparse covering on the earth

explanation.surface: Light snow has fallen, leaving scattered flakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scarce; a light snowfall literally covers the earth sparsely.

clue.text: Time to go back and work for publisher

indicators.note: telling the word for time to go back means it is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Eastertide or 'time and tide'

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break and then returns to a job at a publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns TIDE into EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing, preparing text for print, is the core job done for a publisher.

clue.text: Picture that's put on outside of publication

indicators.note: the letters for the first piece are placed around the outside of the word for publication, wrapping it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, 'that is'
a mag is a magazine, a periodical publication

explanation.surface: A photograph is printed on the cover of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as 'that is', abbreviated IE; its I and E go either side of MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a visual representation, the same thing as an image.

clue.text: Viola, say, in Tchaikovsky's first success

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: a win is a success

explanation.surface: A violist enjoys a triumph playing Tchaikovsky's First.
explanation.walkthrough: Viola looks like the instrument, but she is the heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, whose brother Sebastian is her double.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola in Twelfth Night has a brother born at the same birth, so she is an example of one of a pair of siblings.

clue.text: Council member's corrupt deal initially repels island

indicators.note: corrupt here means spoiled or debased, so the letters are rearranged
initially asks for only the first letter of repels

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A councillor's crooked deal is at first rejected by an island community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges DEAL plus R (the start of 'repels', from 'initially') into ALDER. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior elected member of a borough or city council.

clue.text: Intimidating person removes one head of operations from railroad

indicators.note: removes says a letter is taken out of the longer word that follows 'from'

parts.note: to dragoon someone is to railroad or coerce them into something

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of operations

explanation.surface: A bully takes charge of running the railway, ousting the chief of operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is a link: one letter, the O at the head of 'operations', comes out of DRAGOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, forbidding person, especially a stern older woman, is called a dragon.

clue.text: Incompetent soldiers made fewer advances

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
an advance is a loan, so making fewer of them is lending less

explanation.surface: Inept troops moved forward less often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' suggests military progress, but here it means loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any skill or aptitude makes a person incompetent.

clue.text: Like the mistakes in Shakespearean comedy

definitions.text: Like the mistakes in Shakespearean comedy

parts.words: Like the mistakes in Shakespearean comedy
parts.note: Shakespeare's farce about two pairs of twins is titled after the slips and confusions it is full of

explanation.walkthrough: The play is The Comedy of Errors.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything mistaken, as the blunders in The Comedy of Errors are.

clue.text: Vessel requiring a mast to be replaced

indicators.note: replaced means placed again in a different arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A ship needs a new mast fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' looks like part of the instruction, but it belongs in the fodder; 'requiring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by steam engines is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Barbaric type irritated horse

parts.note: something that got to you, or simply got you, irritated you
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A savage warrior's mount is in a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like the animal, but it is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were a Germanic people who sacked Rome, so the word has long meant an uncivilised barbarian.

clue.text: Stand in Paddington, for example

definitions.meaning: to stand something is to put up with or tolerate it
Paddington is the marmalade-loving animal from Peru in Michael Bond's children's books

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a position at Paddington, a London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington looks like the London station, but it is the children's book character. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a famous fictional example of the furry animal, and 'stand' means tolerate.

clue.text: Unconvincing, like moon rock brought back to earth?

definitions.meaning: a story that is hard to believe or improbable

definitions.text: like moon rock brought back to earth?
definitions.meaning: rock samples were carried a great distance home from the moon

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that moon rock was really returned to Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implausible seems to have been reached for from a long way off, hence improbable; moon rock was literally collected from far away.

clue.text: Reportedly subscribed to domed building

indicators.note: reportedly says the words for the first part are said aloud, not spelt

parts.note: to subscribe is literally to write beneath, so subscribed to means wrote under

explanation.surface: A building with a dome was said to have been funded by subscribers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscribed' means signed beneath, so 'wrote under', which in a non-rhotic accent sounds like ROTUNDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically topped with a dome.

clue.text: Hamlet, for example, where English maiden keeps animal for riding

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the first pair of letters wraps around the animal

parts.note: in cricket a maiden over, one with no runs, is abbreviated M
a pony is a small horse ridden especially by children

explanation.surface: In a village somewhere in England, a young woman stables a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests a small village, but it is the Shakespeare play named after its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a character whose name is the title of the play, which makes him a name-giver to the work.

clue.text: Subdued as the wind may be

definitions.meaning: the wind section of an orchestra can be played with a mute

explanation.surface: The wind can be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted means softened or restrained; wind instruments are muted with a device in the bell.

clue.text: Wrinkled old hat?

definitions.meaning: old hat means hackneyed or out of date

explanation.surface: Someone describes a creased, battered old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn by long use is both creased by age and stale from overuse.

clue.text: It's said the king can't do it, mistakenly

definitions.text: It's said the king can't do it
definitions.meaning: the saying goes that the king can do no ill

explanation.surface: The king can't do it properly, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'the king can do no wrong' fits the first; 'mistakenly' is the adverbial sense, as in 'guessed it badly'.

clue.text: Some gaze round, hiding nothing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People looking around find nothing hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding nothing' reads as one phrase about honesty, but 'hiding' links the wordplay to the definition 'nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought, the figure for nothing at all, is a synonym.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty associated with old dance

parts.note: the Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907

explanation.surface: An ancient Chinese court is linked with a traditional dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Head denied extra payment for responsibility

indicators.note: the head of the word is denied, so its first letter is taken away

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment on top of wages

explanation.surface: A boss refuses staff an extra payment, citing accountability.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty that falls on someone is their responsibility.

clue.text: Handicapped, but did without second point in game

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word did goes around the other pieces

parts.note: in tennis, advantage is the point won after deuce

explanation.surface: A player was hampered but still managed without a second point in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but it means 'outside' here. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disadvantaged means being held back or impaired, as a handicap does.
